chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from al-Mu‘allā ibn Abī Shihāb, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Ḥasan asked the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him and his family), “O father! What is the reward for those who come to your Ziyārah?” He replied, “O my son! Whoever came to my Ziyārah while I was alive or after my death, or came to the Ziyārah of your father, it will be an obligation upon Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic, that I go to their Ziyārah on the Day of Judgment, and I will deliver them from their sins.”

key_terms.أَزُورَهُ: I will visit him (referring to the Prophet visiting the visitor on Judgment Day)
key_terms.حَقّاً عَلَى اللَّهِ: An obligation upon God (a theological concept where God is bound by His promise to reward)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation or pilgrimage to the shrine of an Imam or Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyārah to the Prophet and his family?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the concept of *Haqq Allah* (a divine obligation) rather than mere reward, emphasizing the Prophet’s intercessory role in purifying the visitor's sins. It underscores the spiritual continuity between the Prophet and Imam al-Hasan, affirming that visiting either constitutes a direct engagement with the Ahl al-Bayt’s sanctity, a core tenet in Shia devotional practice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from Mu’allā ibn Abī Shihāb, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq), who said:

Ḥasan (ibn ‘Ali (a.s.)) asked the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.), “O father! What is the reward for those who come to your Ziyārah?” The Prophet (s.a.a.w.) replied, “O my son! On the Day of Judgment, it will be my obligation toward Allah to go to the Ziyārah of those who had come to my Ziyārah, during my life or after my death, or had come to the Ziyārah of your father, and to save them from their sins.”
